open_blockers: DATA-DEC-03'S SERVICE PATH IS DECIDED IN PART AND NOT YET IN EFFECT; WHAT REMAINS IS A1'S, WP-0A-DB-00'S AND THE INTEGRATION OWNER'S, NOT THIS PACKAGE'S (heading made to match the body 2026-10-07 on C0 F5; it read "A1'S AND THE INTEGRATION OWNER'S"). CORRECTED 2026-10-06 BY A0 (/claude/a0_atlas): the previous text said the service path was undecided and that "the only member of app_worker is postgres". Both stopped being true on main: RFC-2026-028 (the worker identity, Approved 2026-10-05) decides the identity, and db/foundation/migrations/173_worker_login_identity.sql creates app_worker_login and grants it app_worker WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE, ADMIN FALSE, so on a migrate-clean cluster app_worker has two members, postgres and app_worker_login. Still open, each by RFC-2026-028's status line and migration 173's header: A1's acceptance as DATA-DEC-03's co-owner; credential custody (Q-028-3) before the provisioned instance gets a credential; the platform pooler measurement (Q-028-12, with Q170-c); 173 is declared pending on the provisioned instance; and no service cell's policy exists until its own batch lands, so app_worker reads and writes no row of any forced table. Also still open by RFC-2026-028's status line (added 2026-10-07 on A1 F2): A1R-2 with A1-173-1, the PRODUCTION worker runner's checks -- refuse a job transaction whose app.workspace_id is neither null nor empty after set local role app_worker, and refuse unless current_user = session_user = 'app_worker_login' with no pg_db_role_setting row for the role -- owed to the batch that writes the runner (RFC-2026-026's worker half); and §5/5's secret-scan half, NOT implemented (the repository secret scan does not name a migration password or verifier literal), owed to the Integration Owner's path. The referral this package made is discharged; the remainder of the question belongs to A1, WP-0A-DB-00 and the Integration Owner, and this package must not infer an answer to it (evidence/WP-0A-A0-006/author-reverify-2026-10-06.md §4). Text as recorded: DATA-DEC-03 IS CLOSED ONLY AS FAR AS RFC-2026-016 §4 STATES, AND THE PART IT TURNS ON IS STILL OPEN. This blocker used to read that the decision was referred to A1 and unanswered, which was true when written and stopped being true on 2026-09-05: RFC-2026-016 closed it to the extent §4 states and RFC-2026-017 records that closure. What remains open is the service path, which RFC-2026-016 §4 says in terms is undecided and RFC-2026-022 §5/8 measures as not in effect -- the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses row level security. So the referral is discharged and the QUESTION is not, and it is still A1's to answer rather than this package's to infer.
